contests.title: St. Petersburg — No. 1 Referendum: Water and stormwater bonds

provenance.quote: Shall the City finance storm resilience improvements, including but not limited to, floodwater protection, stormwater pump stations, drainage infrastructure, as well as wastewater collection and treatment facilities, drinking water distribution and supply facilities, by issuing general obligation bonds in one or more series, not exceeding $600,000,000, bearing interest not exceeding maximum legal rates, maturing not more than 30 years from each issuance date, pledging the City's full faith, credit, and unlimited ad valorem taxing power?

contests.title: St. Petersburg — No. 1 Charter Amendment: Jamestown vacant lots

provenance.quote: The City Charter Park and Waterfront Map contains a composite parcel identified as “Jamestown” composed of: Unity Park, recreational open space within Jamestown apartments, and nine City-owned lots in the adjacent neighborhood that are vacant and closed to the public. Shall the City Charter be amended to remove those nine vacant lots from the Map to allow subsequent / separate land use changes and potential sale of those lots for affordable or workforce housing?

contests.title: St. Petersburg — No. 2 Referendum: Harborage Marina lease

provenance.quote: May City Council approve amendment of the lease of City-owned submerged lands at Harborage Marina subject to conditions in ordinance 640-H? Such amendment would extend the term of the lease to 30 years and require the tenant to construct new improvements at no cost to the City, including 200 linear feet of docks, boat lifts, and expanded restrooms. Those improvements would be owned by the City at the end of the lease.

contests.title: St. Petersburg — No. 2 Charter Amendment: Port lease limit

provenance.quote: The City Charter currently limits leases at the Port of St. Petersburg to 10 years without approval by citywide referendum. Shall the Charter be amended to increase that limitation to 25 years? That amendment would make the Port consistent with adjacent Albert Whitted Airport and provide the City with additional flexibility to enter into agreements with private entities for redevelopment of Port facilities. That amendment would not change the permitted use of the Port.

measures.officialStatement:
Section 1. That Section 3.3, Nomination of Board of Commissioners, Subsection (A), Filing, of the Charter of the City of Madeira Beach shall be amended to read as follows: (A). Filing. Every person who shall desire to become a candidate for nomination under the provisions of this Charter to the office of Mayor and District-Commissioner, shall qualify to become such candidate by filing with the City Clerk during the candidate qualifying period held during the first two full weeks in December June, excluding weekends, beginning at Noon on Monday, the first day of the qualifying period and ending at Noon on Friday, the last day of the qualifying period. Under no circumstances shall the City Clerk accept any nomination petitions or filing fees after the close of the filing period as stated herein. Every person's application is to have his/her name printed upon the ballot as a candidate for nomination to the office for which he/she aspires, in which application, he/she shall declare from the district he/she is a candidate or so declare if he/she is a candidate for Mayor. All applications shall be accompanied by an affidavit the candidate is an elector and a resident of the City of Madeira Beach, Florida, for one (1) year immediately prior to the date of said application and has been a resident of said district for which he/she declares himself/herself to be a candidate for a period of six (6) months prior to the date of said application. With said application shall be filed a petition which shall indicate prominently the district from which the Petitioner is a candidate, or if he/she be a candidate for Mayor.

Section 6. This Ordinance shall take effect immediately upon its passage and adoption, provided, however, it shall not be effective until such is approved by the electorate at a referendum election thereon to ratify the terms and conditions of this Ordinance. That Section 4.8, Induction of Board of Commissioners into Office; Meetings, of the Charter of the City of Madeira Beach shall be amended to read as follows: The first meeting of each newly elected member of the Board of Commissioners for induction into office shall be at a Board of Commissioners meeting to be held on or before the last day of the month in which the election was held and certification thereof. Meetings of the Board of Commissioners shall be open to the public in accordance with the Florida Statutes. Ordinance 2026-07 Page 3 of 5

measures.questionText: In 2022, voters in a citywide referendum approved amendment of the City Charter to reschedule elections for Mayor and Council Members to even-numbered years so that City elections would align with national and state elections beginning in 2024. Shall the Charter be amended to make technical, clarifying, and conforming changes necessary and appropriate to fully effectuate the intent of the 2022 referendum, including alignment of the Charter-review process with the current election schedule?
measures.officialStatement:
(E) Accordingly, the Charter should be amended to make technical, clarifying, and conforming changes that are necessary and appropriate to fully effectuate the 2022 Referendum. Those “cleanup” amendments can be generally described as follows: (1) Charter section 5.05 should be amended to require that municipal primary and gen- eral elections will occur on the same dates as the state primary and general elections. That section should also clarify that, if the state returns to a two-primary system (which it had through 2005 and which recent legislation proposed the rein- troduction of), the municipal primary election will coincide with the first state primary election, rather than the second state primary election (which would be a smaller, runoff election). That approach will ensure that municipal elections remain aligned with state elections regardless of any future change to the schedule for state elections. (2) Charter section 5.05 should also be amended to improve readability (the relevant portions are currently large blocks of text that are difficult to parse) and consistency (with state law and with other provisions of the Charter) and to reflect current prac- tices for administration of elections (e.g., that voting takes place in multiple polling places established by the Pinellas County Supervisor of Elections, rather than a single place established by the City). (3) Charter section 8.01 should be amended to require that the Charter Review Com- mission (“CRC”) will be formed in years ending in nine and that any amendment

00899590 / v03S 3 of 8 Election Schedule Cleanup proposed by CRC will be placed on the ballot of municipal general election in years ending in zero. That approach is consistent with the 2022 Referendum, which moved future elections later by one year to accomplish the transition to even-year elections. (F) Pursuant to Florida Statutes section 166.031, the Charter may be amended pursuant to a referendum put to a vote of the electors at a general election held within the municipality, and a referendum to amend the Charter as described in this section will be held in conjunc- tion with the municipal general election scheduled for November 3, 2026. (G) For the reasons described in these findings, the actions taken by this ordinance serve a valid municipal purpose and are in the best interests of the City, and this ordinance is adopted in consideration of these findings. SECTION 2—DATE OF REFERENDUM: The City Council hereby calls the Charter amendment referendum described in this ordinance (the “Referendum”) to be placed on the ballot of the municipal general election scheduled for November 3, 2026. SECTION 3—FORMATTING CONVENTIONS: With respect to the potential amendment of the Charter set forth in this ordinance, additions are indicated by underlining, deletions are in- dicated by strikethrough text, and unchanged paragraphs omitted for brevity are indicated by three ellipsis dots on a separate line. SECTION 4—CHARTER AMENDMENT: If the Referendum is approved by a majority vote, the City shall file a revised version of the St. Petersburg City Charter with the Florida De- partment of State that will amend the Charter as stated in this section, with those amendments effective upon filing. provenance.quote: In 2022, voters in a citywide referendum approved amendment of the City Charter to reschedule elections for Mayor and Council Members to even-numbered years so that City elections would align with national and state elections beginning in 2024. Shall the Charter be amended to make technical, clarifying, and conforming changes necessary and appropriate to fully effectuate the intent of the 2022 referendum, including alignment of the Charter-review process with the current election schedule?

measures.questionText: Shall the Treasure Island City Charter Section 3.07(c) be amended to require that “a supermajority vote of four members of the board of commissioners shall be required for the approval of any planned developments or special area plans?” This provision will become effective immediately upon approval by the electors or as otherwise provided by law.

provenance.quote: Shall the Treasure Island City Charter Section 3.07(c) be amended to require that “a supermajority vote of four members of the board of commissioners shall be required for the approval of any planned developments or special area plans?” This provision will become effective immediately upon approval by the electors or as otherwise provided by law.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Removes the Town Charter requirement that the Town Commission appoint a planning and zoning board. The question explains that Florida law already requires the town to appoint a local planning agency.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve removing this specific charter requirement; the state-law requirement for a local planning agency remains.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Beginning in 2036, moves the month for establishing the town’s Charter Review Committee from June to May. This gives the committee and town more time before election-office deadlines for proposed charter amendments on the following November general-election ballot.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve establishing the Charter Review Committee in May instead of June beginning in 2036.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed change to the committee’s start month.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Sets March 15 as the first day candidate petitions for mayor and City Commission are available in a regular city-election year. For a special election, the City Commission would choose the date, under Ordinance 2025-24.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the March 15 regular-election date and a Commission-selected special-election date for making candidate petitions available.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed candidate-petition date amendment.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Moves regular municipal elections from March to the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November and removes the exception for holding city elections with the presidential-preference primary. Districts One and Two continue in even-numbered years and Districts Three and Four in odd-numbered years. This is part of a three-question package: Ordinance 2026-07 takes effect only if all three questions pass.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the November election schedule as part of the package that requires all three questions to pass.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this question; under the ordinance, defeat of any one of the three questions prevents the package from taking effect.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Moves municipal candidate qualifying from the first two full weeks in December to the first two full weeks in June, excluding weekends. It begins at noon on the first Monday and ends at noon on the final Friday. Ordinance 2026-07 takes effect only if all three city questions pass.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the June qualifying period as part of the package that requires all three questions to pass.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this question; under the ordinance, defeat of any one of the three questions prevents the package from taking effect.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Extends District Three and Four commissioners’ terms from March 2027 until the November 2027 election results are certified and successors installed. It extends District One and Two commissioners’ and the mayor-commissioner’s terms from March 2028 until the November 2028 results are certified and successors installed. It also updates the start and installation of new terms to account for election certification. Ordinance 2026-07 takes effect only if all three city questions pass.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve these temporary term extensions and certification-related procedures as part of the package that requires all three questions to pass.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this question; under the ordinance, defeat of any one of the three questions prevents the package from taking effect.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Changes commissioners’ terms of office from two years to three years.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject changing commissioner terms from two years to three years.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: If Question One passes, makes the mayor’s term following the 2027 general election two years instead of the usual three years. This one-time change is intended to maintain staggered terms for the mayor and commissioners.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the two-year mayoral term following the 2027 election, only if Question One also passes.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed conditional change to the mayor’s 2027 term.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes up to $600 million in general obligation bonds, issued in one or more series, for storm resilience, flood protection and stormwater, wastewater and drinking-water improvements. Each series would mature within 30 years of issuance and bear interest no higher than the legal maximum. The city would pledge its full faith and credit and its power to levy property taxes without a stated millage cap to repay the bonds.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the bonds for the listed improvements, with the stated amount, interest and maturity limits and property-tax pledge.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Removes nine city-owned vacant lots, currently closed to the public, from the Charter’s Park and Waterfront Map. The lots are part of the composite Jamestown parcel, which also includes Unity Park and recreational open space at Jamestown apartments. Removing these nine lots would allow later, separate land-use changes and a possible sale for affordable or workforce housing. The question itself does not make those later land-use changes or sell the lots.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve removing the nine vacant lots from the map so later land-use and possible housing-sale decisions can be considered separately.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject removing these nine lots from the Charter map.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows one or more Harborage Marina lease amendments under Ordinance 640-H, each requiring at least six City Council votes. The first amendment must be fully executed by December 31, 2027, or this authority expires. The lease could last no more than 30 years from that first amendment’s effective date and could not expand the leased area. The tenant must build, at no city cost, 200 linear feet of docks with fire-suppression, water and electric service, new boat lifts and expanded restrooms. The city receives ownership of these improvements when the lease expires or ends earlier. Amendments must remain consistent with applicable referendum conditions, with later referendums controlling any conflict.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize the Council to approve the lease amendments within the stated deadline, voting threshold, term, area and construction conditions.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Raises the Port of St. Petersburg’s lease limit without another citywide referendum from ten years to 25 years. A lease within the new limit would still require at least six City Council votes. The amendment does not change the Port’s permitted uses. If voters approve, the charter change takes effect when the revised charter is filed with the state.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the 25-year lease limit with the six-vote Council approval requirement and unchanged permitted uses.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject raising this lease limit from ten years to 25 years.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Updates the Charter to carry out the 2022 decision to hold city elections in even-numbered years. City primaries and general elections would use state election dates; if the state has two primaries, the city uses the earlier one. It updates election-notice and administration wording. The ten-year charter-review process would begin in years ending in nine, with proposed amendments voted on in years ending in zero. In the year ending in nine, the mayor and Council must establish the standard application form by August 1, appointments must be made by September 15, and the review commission must organize in November. The review report is due in the year ending in zero by the earlier of July 31 or 15 days before the last regular Council meeting before the ballot-submission deadline. Voter-approved changes take effect when the revised charter is filed with the state.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve these election-administration and charter-review timing changes to implement the even-year schedule.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Requires four members of the Board of Commissioners to vote yes to approve any planned development or special area plan. The provision would take effect immediately upon voter approval, or as otherwise provided by law.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve requiring four affirmative Commission votes for these development and special-area plans.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed four-vote approval requirement.
